newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee weakens as central bank buys dollars.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee weakens as central bank buys dollars.

text.p: The Indian rupee fell against the dollar in afternoon trade as the central bank dollar bought dollars, dealers said.
They said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) bought forward dollars at various levels.
"They hit June, August and September delivery dollars," one dealer at a foreign bank said.
The amount of intervention was unclear.
"I think what is more important is the the RBI is in the market and has been bidding higher each time," the dealer said.
In latest deals, the dollar was quoted 35.767/7752 rupees, compared with Thursday's close of 35.74/75.
Dealers said the rupee had been stuck in a narrow range between 35.745 and 35.755, but fell rapidly once the RBI came into the market.
The rupee fell to 35.78 at one stage, they said.
They said the State Bank of India had also been a buyer of dollar, but its action was dwarfed by the central bank's buying.
"But RBI's buying has overshadowed their demand," said a dealer.
